# Synthetic native authoring contracts

These fixtures are generated from Chartworks' own isolated PostgreSQL acceptance
fixtures. They contain no customer records, operational identity, credential,
bearer, source SQL, native attempt handle or session token.

- `dataset-prepare-contract.json` contains a reviewed-dataset projection and the
  exact frontend Prepare request, checked by both Node and the native closed API
  schema tests. The authored title is also the required descriptive `question`;
  this does not invoke a model or natural-language query engine.
- `dataset-native-public.json` records public DTOs from the real native authoring
  and retained-delivery services. The `private` flags exercise actor-private
  application behavior inside the synthetic fixture. Run IDs, observation times
  and digests belong to that test execution, not a deployed user report.

## Provenance

`test/acceptance/source_support_test.go` creates a fresh test schema and inserts
literal sample rows. In particular, the recorded exact amount is the sum of the
hard-coded values `9007199254740993.125` and `5.5`:
`9007199254740998.625`. These deliberately exceed ordinary floating-point exactness
so formatting cannot hide a numeric-custody defect. The approved native format
may round the displayed label; raw digits remain available in retained details.

`test/acceptance/topic_drafts_test.go` constructs the literal synthetic
`topic-source` / `commerce` topic and its reviewed `revenue` measure. Dataset,
context and binding identifiers are generated by the same production metadata
code under test. `source_support_test.go` and `security_support_test.go` create
only test identities and test authorization envelopes; credentials are excluded
from the recorded public DTO projection.

`TestReportAppDeterministicPreparation` in
`test/acceptance/report_app_prepare_test.go` executes the bounded native path,
checks query/model counts and optionally writes the public DTOs to
`CHARTWORKS_DATASET_FIXTURE_PATH`. A recursive export guard rejects SQL, native
control and credential fields before writing. Use the repository's documented
native/isolated PostgreSQL test setup, then run that exact acceptance test with
an output path outside the source tree. Review the regenerated diff and rerun
both native schema and frontend contracts before replacing a fixture.

The browser fixture also carries an independently captured continuous journey
with initial/final report reads. Its report, page, widget and retained-run
coordinates must remain consistent: never relabel an immutable retained result
to fit a test. Test-only UUID sequencing is allowed in the synthetic frame;
production ID generation and host authority are unchanged.

These recordings qualify DTO interoperability and synthetic host behavior. They
do not establish real Pengui admission, deployed authorization or provider use.
